factText: The scaly-foot snail is metal - literally! Instead of a garden, these snails live on deep sea hydrothermal vents. Using iron and sulphur that these vents spew out, they build iron plate armour on their shell and soft tissue. They're the only animals known to utilize iron sulphide in this way!

factText: Bird lungs are strange. Instead of pumping air in and out of a sack (terribly inefficient), their lungs are like a tube where air can flow constantly in one direction. There is evidence that some dinosaur lungs are also like this.
Gherkin slugs are a thing! They're only found in New Zealand, and eat fungi and algae.
